answer: Each agent must bond scarce, nontransferable work credits before it can submit jobs, and the protocol releases those credits only after randomly sampled counterparties attest that the work passed a reproducible check. A tundra node, harbor operator, or delta-market newcomer faces the same rule: spinning up identities does not multiply voting weight, because each bond is locked and each failed audit burns part of it. An attacker must therefore acquire real credits and risk losing them on every fabricated identity.
